::: {#exm-compute-bound}

#### A slow rate is not the problem

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
slow_run = train_and_score(512, 0.03, 0, n_epochs=100)
long_rates = [0.1, 0.3, 1]
long_scores = [train_and_score(512, lr, 0, n_epochs=100)[-1] for lr in long_rates]
best_long_tuned = max(long_scores)
print(slow_run[19], slow_run[-1], long_scores)
# Stop the render if the prose below stops being true.
assert slow_run[-1] - slow_run[19] > seed_high - seed_low
assert slow_run[-1] < at_20
assert all(s < l for s, l in zip(slow_run[19:], long_run[19:]))
assert best_long_tuned - at_20 < seed_high - seed_low
```

::: {#fig-compute-bound}

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "Validation accuracy against epoch, from 1 to 100, for width 512 at learning rates 0.03 and the best rate from the sweep. The best-rate curve is flat near 0.95 after epoch 20. The 0.03 curve starts lower, rises slowly from about 0.88 at epoch 20 to about 0.91 at epoch 100, below the other curve from epoch 20 on."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
ax.plot(range(1, 101), long_run, label=f"learning rate {best_rate[512]}");
ax.plot(range(1, 101), slow_run, label="learning rate 0.03");
ax.axvline(20, linestyle="--", color="gray");
ax.set_xlabel("epoch");
ax.set_ylabel("validation accuracy");
ax.legend();
fig.tight_layout();
plt.show()
```

Validation [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) after each [epoch](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) of 100-epoch runs of [width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) 512 at two [learning rates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate);
the dashed line marks epoch 20.

:::

At [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) 0.03,
[width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) 512's validation [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) rises from `r sprintf("%.3f", py$slow_run[[20]])` after 20 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch)
to `r sprintf("%.3f", py$slow_run[[100]])` after 100.
That run alone would suggest that 20 epochs hold the model back.
But at its best learning rate the network gets `r sprintf("%.3f", py$at_20)` in 20 epochs,
more than the slow run gets in 100.
Tuned for 100 epochs instead,
over [learning rates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) 0.1, 0.3 and 1,
the best 100-epoch run reaches `r sprintf("%.3f", py$best_long_tuned)`,
less above the 20-epoch run than the seed alone moved width 64 in @sol-seed-spread.
Longer training does not help,
so training this network on these `r py$n_train` images is not [compute-bound](#def-compute-bound).
Something other than training time limits it.

:::
